Notes: Jews permitted to reside at Nevers in the 12th century on payment of 5 sous per family and 20 sous per person (year = midpoint of century); no count
Pope Innocent III protested to Count Hervé of Nevers over the favorable conditions granted to the Jews of his town and county; organized presence, no count
Count Robert expelled the Jews from his county (county-wide expulsion; Population not set to 0 since source does not state none remained in the town)
Louis X authorized the return of the Jews to Nevers; no count
Jews expelled from France; some Nevers Jews took refuge in Provence (Moses of Nevers at Arles 1464; Solomon of Nevers at Tarascon 1494)
Jewish merchants visiting Nevers markets and fairs were forbidden to trade there (council of state 19 April 1740); visitors not residents
A synagogue perhaps of the 14th century stood at 5 rue de la Revenderie (formerly rue des Juifs); year = approximate 14th-century midpoint

Nièvre department only: 123 Jewish deportees 1939-1945 commemorated by plaque unveiled 2012; department-wide 1940 prefecture count 204 Jews and 1942 list 195 individuals (not Nevers-only). Roundup 13 July 1942
